clue.text: Pessimistic forecast from Irishman, as a rule

parts.note: Murphy is a stock Irish surname, here in the possessive since the rule is his
a law is a rule or principle

explanation.surface: A gloomy prediction offered, in general, by a man from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy's law says that anything that can go wrong will; the clue reads it literally as an Irishman's rule.
explanation.definitionFit: The adage predicts that whatever can go wrong will go wrong, a gloomy expectation of events.

clue.text: Some money, partly in note form

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of some cash comes as a banknote.
explanation.definitionFit: A memo is a brief written message, a short record.

clue.text: Is as different in race as a foreigner

indicators.note: in tells us the rearranged letters sit inside the word for race

parts.note: a run is a race

indicators.note: different signals that the letters of is and as take a new form

explanation.surface: Being of another ethnicity makes someone an outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' looks like ethnicity in the surface, but it is a running contest; 'different' scrambles IS AS before 'in' sets it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A national of Russia is a foreigner from the British point of view.

clue.text: Tavern? Bills are checked there

parts.note: a tavern is a public house where the bill is checked; here the house is the upper chamber of Parliament where proposed laws are scrutinised

explanation.surface: In a pub, the tab is verified before paying.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, the House of Lords is the upper chamber of Parliament, which revises Bills passed by the Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper chamber of the UK Parliament examines and amends draft legislation.

clue.text: Master is snooping about, as they say? Thar's a revelation

indicators.note: as they say tells us the words are spoken, and the spoken form gives the answer

parts.note: sir is a master, and pries means is snooping about

explanation.surface: The headmaster poking around discovers something astonishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unexpected and eye-opening comes as a shock or eye-opener.

clue.text: Difficult moment for Cockney passion

indicators.note: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, drop their initial aitches, so both words lose H

parts.note: hard means difficult
an hour is a moment, as in 'the hour has come'

explanation.surface: A Londoner goes through a tough time with strong feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech drops the H, so HARD HOUR becomes 'ARD 'OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is intense enthusiasm or fervour.

clue.text: Midnight service for foreign noble

parts.note: the middle letter of the word night is G
the RAF (Royal Air Force) is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A late-night church service attended by an aristocrat from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midnight' is read as the middle of 'night', its letter G; 'service' suggests a church but means a military arm.
explanation.definitionFit: Graf is the German title equivalent to count or earl, a continental nobleman.

clue.text: Make easier to stop investment

explanation.surface: Simplify matters so as to halt putting money in.
explanation.walkthrough: An investment in old military language is a siege; to relieve a besieged town is to end it.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve is to ease pain or trouble, and also to raise a siege by driving off the besiegers.

clue.text: Throw from speeding mount

parts.note: flying means moving very fast
a mare is a female horse, a mount

explanation.surface: A rider is thrown from a horse going at full gallop.
explanation.definitionFit: In wrestling, it is a move where the opponent is seized by the arm and hurled over the shoulder.

clue.text: Forced to include square-dancing in the ball

indicators.note: to include means the word for forced holds the next piece within it

parts.note: if someone is made to do something, they are forced to

indicators.note: dancing letters are moving about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Guests are compelled to take part in square-dancing at a formal party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square-dancing' reads as one folk dance, but the hyphen hides an anagram: 'dancing' scrambles 'square', and 'to include' places that inside the word for forced.
explanation.definitionFit: A masquerade is a ball at which guests wear masks and costumes.

clue.text: Perform melody on piano

indicators.note: in an across clue, melody placed on piano means it follows it

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
a lay is a song or melody

explanation.surface: A musician is asked to perform a tune at the keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To play is to perform music or a part on stage.

clue.text: Earl's seat

parts.note: a seat is a country house of a noble family or something to sit on; an earl lent his title to a padded sofa

explanation.definitionFit: The deep-buttoned leather sofa is named after an earl who commissioned one.

clue.text: Weapon taking toll

explanation.surface: A spear-like arm exacts a heavy price.
explanation.definitionFit: A pike is a long infantry spear; it is also short for turnpike, a road charge paid at a gate.

clue.text: Uncouth as a hooligan when disorderly

parts.note: a rough is a violent, rowdy person

indicators.note: disorderly signals that the letters of the word when are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is as rude as a lout whenever they are unruly.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough-hewn means crudely shaped, and figuratively lacking refinement or polish.

clue.text: It's not clear I am fair

parts.note: I'm is the short form of I am
fair means adequate, passable

explanation.surface: Someone says it is unclear whether they are just.
explanation.definitionFit: A road that is blocked cannot be crossed, so it is not clear.

clue.text: Display what's provided in, say. Main Street?

indicators.note: in tells us the word for provided goes inside the other piece
say tells us the street name is taken by its spoken form

parts.note: Main St, the usual short form, spoken out loud resembles mane-st
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what is laid out on show along the high road of a town.
explanation.walkthrough: Main St is the written short form of Main Street; 'say' takes it as heard, mane-st, and 'in' places the word for provided within that sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To manifest is to show or reveal plainly, as an adjective obvious.

clue.text: Match points referred back to judge

indicators.note: referred back means the whole run of letters is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a meet is a sporting fixture or match
S and E are compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: In a contest, scores are passed back to the umpire for a ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'referred back' turns MEETSE round, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem is to regard or consider, as in 'I esteem it an honour', a sense of assessing.

clue.text: Pick a roller coaster to sit on

parts.note: the pick of the bunch is the best
a roller coaster is a fairground ride

explanation.surface: Choose a fairground attraction to sit astride.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestride is to straddle, sitting with legs either side.

clue.text: Order to start shooting in battle

explanation.surface: A command to open fire during combat.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the film director's call to begin filming, not to fire weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: A director calls this word to begin filming a scene; it also means military combat, as in killed in it.

clue.text: Like the sound of CD player?

definitions.text: Like the sound of CD player?

parts.words: Like the sound of CD player?
parts.note: C and D are two musical notes, so a player sounding them produces a pair of notes

explanation.surface: A question about how a compact disc machine sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: CD suggests a compact disc, but it is read as the notes C and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-tone describes something with two colours or two notes, like a two-note siren.

clue.text: Criminal who's relatively unblessed?

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker is less fortunate than others.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says it is more blessed to give than to receive, so one who takes is less blessed by comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence who handles stolen goods is a criminal of this name; and one who takes rather than gives is less blessed, per the proverb.

clue.text: Flower girl embracing boy

indicators.note: embracing means the girl's name wraps round the boy's

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name
Ben is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A florist's daughter hugging a lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbena is a garden plant with clusters of small blooms.

clue.text: All that's needed to upset somebody — yuk!

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: one means somebody, as in 'one does one's best'
ugh is an exclamation of disgust like yuk

explanation.surface: Just enough to disgust someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ONE up to give ENO.
explanation.definitionFit: Enough means a sufficient quantity, as much as is required.

clue.text: Attachment on weapon works — don't change it

indicators.note: change it tells us to alter the order of the letters in the words just before

explanation.surface: A fitting on a sword functions well, so leave it alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't change it' looks like advice to leave things be, but 'change it' rearranges WORKS DONT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword-knot is a ribbon or tassel tied to a sword hilt.

clue.text: Chess manoeuvre supporting king

parts.note: if you are for something, you support it
K is the chess notation for king

explanation.surface: A chess move made in defence of the king.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, this is an attack by one piece on two of the opponent's pieces at once.

clue.text: Odd bits of culture, such as this

indicators.note: odd bits means the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the word

explanation.surface: Scraps of cultural knowledge, of the kind used here.
explanation.definitionFit: Each item solved in a crossword is a hint of this sort.

clue.text: Wind-sock

explanation.surface: The airfield's cloth cone for showing the breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: Blow means to move as air does in a gale; it is also a punch, as is a sock.

clue.text: Special bulletin about the Spanish that signals bad news

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the word for the Spanish
special suggests something made differently, so the word bulletin is rearranged

parts.note: el is the Spanish definite article

explanation.surface: An extra news report concerning Spain announces a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' scrambles 'bulletin' and 'about' wraps it round the Spanish article. The Lutine bell hangs at Lloyd's of London, the insurance market; it was rung to announce a ship's loss.
explanation.definitionFit: At the London insurance market, this bell was traditionally struck once for a lost vessel, twice for good tidings.

clue.text: Toothless philanthropist vanishes into the garden

indicators.note: vanishes says the philanthropist's name drops out of the longer word

parts.note: edentate means having no teeth
Henry Tate, the sugar magnate, gave his art collection and the gallery that bears his name to the nation

explanation.surface: A gumless benefactor disappears among the flower beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toothless' looks like a description of the philanthropist, but it is the word to cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the paradise where Adam and Eve lived is known as this garden.

clue.text: Hackneyed yarn, lacking detail

parts.note: thread is spun yarn
bare means plain, unadorned, without detail

explanation.surface: A tired old story with no specifics in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' suggests a tale, fitting the surface, but it means spun fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare is worn thin, figuratively stale and overused.
